USMLE-style practice · Pathology

A clearance signal on a dying cell

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A macrophage recognizes an apoptotic cell before extensive leakage of its cytoplasmic contents. Recognition is promoted by exposure of a phospholipid normally concentrated on the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane. Which molecule supplies this clearance signal?

  1. Triglyceride
  2. Glycogen
  3. Hemoglobin
  4. Phosphatidylserine
  5. Cholesterol ester
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Phosphatidylserine

Externalized phosphatidylserine acts as an eat-me signal during apoptotic clearance.

Understanding the options

Phosphatidylserine
Externalized phosphatidylserine acts as an eat-me signal during apoptotic clearance.
Cholesterol ester
Cholesterol esters are stored lipids, not the classic leaflet-flipping signal.
Triglyceride
Triglycerides are neutral storage lipids.
Glycogen
Glycogen is a carbohydrate storage polymer.
Hemoglobin
Hemoglobin is an erythrocyte protein rather than a membrane phospholipid signal.
